title: Hazavittem, eladtam, eltettem: Finishing the Story

sections.title: Prefixes that answer "what did you do with it"
sections.content: A small family of prefixed verbs exists just to answer Mit csináltál vele?: hazavisz ("take/carry home" — built on the visz you already know: vittem, vitted, vitte...), elad ("to sell" — built on regular ad), and eltesz ("to put away" — built on the tesz stem you already know: tettem, tetted, tette...). Each keeps the exact same personal endings as its bare verb; the prefix just adds the direction or outcome.

sections.title: What happened to it
rows: I got a gift from Károly.

items.spanish: Megtaláltam a kulcsomat, aztán hazavittem a táskát.
items.english: I found my key, then took the bag home.

items.spanish: Nem kellett a régi kabát, ezért eladtam.
items.english: I didn't need the old coat, so I sold it.

items.spanish: Eltettem a számlát, ha esetleg kell még.
items.english: I put the receipt away in case I still need it.

sections.content: -tól/-től never assimilates the way -val/-vel does — Károlytól is always Károlytól, whatever consonant Károly ended in, so it's one less thing to double-check than instrumental forms are.
